Customer: acme_integration: we're hitting a 413 when calling /v1/rerank. payload is ~120 docs, each ~3-4k chars. error just says 'Payload Too Large'. can you advise?
Jenny (Support): can you paste the request body or a sanitized curl + the exact error response? that helps triage.
Customer: here's a redacted curl (docs array trimmed):
```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"How do I reset password?","docs":[{"id":"1","text":"<long doc>"}, {"id":"2","text":"<long doc>"}, ... up to 120 items]}'
```
Error body: `{"error":"Payload Too Large","code":413}`
SupportBot: automated-detection: estimated token counts - query_tokens=250, docs_tokens=41234, total_tokens≈41484. rerank hard limit ~= 32768 tokens. suggest chunking docs or truncating long docs.
Arjun (ML Eng): quick context — the rerank endpoint runs a joint scoring pass which concatenates query+doc text (per doc) during scoring; there are service-side limits to avoid OOM across batches. when total token footprint per request crosses ~32k we currently return 413.
Arjun (ML Eng): short workarounds: 1) prefilter with a cheap embedding-based nearest-neighbors (send query to embeddings, pick top 50 docs) then call rerank; 2) truncate document text server-side to first N characters/tokens (ideally preserve the part most relevant to search); 3) send docs in multiple smaller requests (batching).
Customer: is there a recommended docs-per-request number? we need approximate guidance so we can change client quickly.
Arjun (ML Eng): it depends on doc length, but with average doc ~3k chars (~500 tokens) you hit the limit around 60-70 docs. if docs are longer reduce to 20-30. safer rule: ensure total estimated tokens < 28k to leave headroom.
Sam (Platform): can you share a small repro script so we can run it against staging and confirm behavior? also we'll want exact sizes to reproduce.
Customer: attaching quick node repro (sanitized):
```\nconst fetch = require('node-fetch');\nconst docs = Array.from({length:120}).map((_,i)=>({id:i+1,text: 'x'.repeat(3200)}));\nfetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank',{method:'POST',headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer $TOK','Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({query:'reset password',docs})}).then(r=>r.text()).then(console.log).catch(console.error);\n```
Jenny (Support): thanks — we'll run this in staging. i'm also capturing the customer's ask: improve the 413 body to include which field caused the breach (e.g., total_tokens, docs_count, doc_examples) and a short recommended mitigation string. that would save time for customers. cc @Nora (Product)
Nora (Product): :thinking: agree this is a frequent support pain. can you add the exact payload we used and the staging response? we should propose a small API change: return 413 with JSON `{error:"payload_too_large", reason:"total_tokens_exceeded", total_tokens:NNN, limit:LLLL, suggestion:"use embeddings prefilter or split docs"}`.
Arjun (ML Eng): implementation notes — we already compute token estimates at edge. exposing the counts should be low-risk. prefer to surface both `total_tokens` and `docs_count`. presenting per-doc tokens might be noisy; include `largest_doc_tokens` to help.
Jenny (Support): created internal ticket INF-1123 and added repro + customer repro script. ETA ask from customer?
Customer: if we can get a short-term guideline and a clearer error message in the next 2 weeks that would be great. long term, a server-side automatic chunking fallback would be ideal.
Sam (Platform): short-term: we'll update docs + add an example prefilter pipeline (embedding -> top-K -> rerank). i'll coordinate with docs and send a PR today.
Nora (Product): i'll prioritize the error payload change for the next minor release — will update on ETA in INF-1123. thanks for the repro, team.
Customer: awesome, thanks all :+1: this will unblock our rollout.
Jenny (Support): marking this resolved for now; will follow up in the ticket with timeline.
